result.title: When May a Bandit Leave Its Anchor? E-Process-Authorized Thompson Sampling under Non-stationarity
result.comment: 25 pages, 3 figures. Accepted to the E-Values Workshop at NeurIPS 2026 (poster)
result.summary: Stationarity rewards memory, but after a change the same history can mislead. We ask when forgetting should be permitted. E-process-authorized Thompson sampling (e-ATS) gives each arm full-history and discounted Beta states. An anytime-valid e-process first authorizes the discounted state, then a reversible relevance score controls its influence. Before authorization, e-ATS exactly follows optimistic Thompson sampling (OTS). Under a Beta-Bernoulli prior-predictive stationary model, e-ATS's probability of ever departing from OTS is at most the chosen $α_E$, without fitted thresholds. Relative to e-ATS, removing authorization increased mean normalized dynamic pseudo-regret by $38.4\%$ on the registered suite but reduced it by $7.5\%$ on the literature-derived replay suite. Therefore, evidence controls when adaptation begins, not whether it always helps.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究非平稳 bandit 中何时允许遗忘历史，提出用 anytime-valid e-process 先“授权”折扣后的 Beta 状态，再以可逆相关性分数控制其影响，从而在原则上精确遵循乐观 Thompson 采样，并保证偏离概率不超过 α_E。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「何时用证据授权切换状态、如何控制旧状态影响」的机制，可能与 LVR 中何时从 latent 状态转向新证据、停止决策与证据筛选有概念对照，可供核查。
